analysis:
Scope: documentation change in docs/developer/build.md (date bump at line 3; new CI (dev) hourly row at line 340 and section 'Hourly full run of dev' at lines 342-356) and a test change in scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py (new HOURLY constant at about line 134, workflow classification at 709-710, new test_hourly_full_run_only_dispatches_ci_dev_on_dev at 959-977). The ci-dev-hourly.yml workflow itself is not in the supplied units, so its actual content is unverified. Only the documented behavior and the test's expectations are visible.

Security-relevant behavior: the test asserts the workflow has top-level 'permissions: {}' and a single job on ubuntu-24.04 with only actions:write and contents:read. It also asserts no 'uses:', secrets, checkout, id-token or self-hosted/darkbloom labels. It allows exactly one command, 'gh workflow run ci-dev.yml --repo "$REPOSITORY" --ref dev', skipped when an unfinished dispatched run exists. Together these constrain the token and runner exposure, which improves the guarantee. The one exception is that the test only checks workflow text, not the real workflow.

The workflow does not touch provider assets (A-001..A-020), the coordinator-to-provider boundary or release signing. It is routed to a GitHub-hosted runner, not a Darkbloom or Blacksmith lane, and does not touch release/signing workflows (documented as unaffected). The remaining questions are outside the supplied evidence: whether ci-dev-hourly.yml matches the test (e.g. no injection via inputs/env) and whether dev's ci-dev.yml workflow_dispatch handling is safe. A cost or availability consequence (hourly full CI runs, a possible issue-creation path with write permission) is not in scope of the threat model. No findings. Docs claim 'Paid manual dispatches' are unaffected; nothing here contradicts that.
